# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Three-Zone Model per CLAUDE.loa.md: `.claude/` system = never edit (use `.claude/overrides/` or `.loa.config.yaml`); `grimoires/loa/`, `.beads/` state = read/write; this skill's app zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`) = **Read-only**.

Scope: app-zone files less the `.reviewignore` patterns (read it); `.claude/`, `grimoires/`, `.beads/` and `.run/` are excluded unless `--no-reviewignore` is passed.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->
## Context Discipline

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its
`resources/RETROSPECTIVE.md` (quality gates, sanitization, trajectory logging). Never when the
active skill is continuous-learning itself.
<!-- @skill-include: end retrospective_postlude -->
</retrospective_postlude>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. </documentation_audit>

Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is the cycle-126 sprint-247 PR "full-size adapters, Bridgebuilder and Flatline — every size

forbids. Both dissent voices (Phase 2.5) found all three independently.

fast-gate evidence, which is on its own an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED under this skill. Verification evidence I could

## Observations

### 1. `_ceiling_unverified` is the head entry's flag but gates every hop

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1843` and `:2297` — the flag is computed once from the pre-flight on the head entry, then consulted on every hop's 429 arm (and `:2256` for the context-limit class). Under the `derived` opt-in, a 429 on a fallback hop (whose own probed bound the request may well be under, or which is calibrated) ends the call as `RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED` and records an observation against that fallback entry, instead of walking as before. The arm also treats every 429 the same, including an ordinary requests-per-minute limit that says nothing about the payload (dissent DISS-003/DISS-004/DISS-C-003).
**Suggestion:** Recompute the unverified zone per hop (`estimate > probed_ceiling` of that entry, and not calibrated) or clear the flag when leaving the head entry; consider distinguishing token-limit 429 bodies from RPM ones before refusing to walk.

### 2. `/loa` prints `ceiling: observed -1` from a zero-token observation row

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:811-819` — the jq reduction takes the `min` of `observed_input_tokens` without a positivity check, while cheval writes `observed_input_tokens: 0` when the gate is disabled and the provider message carries no numbers (`head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2005`: `int(_walk_estimate or 0)`). A row `{"observed_input_tokens": 0, "error_class": "PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT"}` yields `obs=0`, which passes the `^[0-9]+$` check, so the status line reads `ceiling: observed -1`. The Python reducer (`ceiling.py:252`) skips non-positive values, so the two readers disagree (dissent DISS-C-004).
**Suggestion:** Filter `observed_input_tokens > 0` in the jq, and do not append a row (or record `null`) when no positive observation exists.

### 3. Observed-bound store has an unlocked read-modify-write

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:279-299` — `load_observed` → append → `os.replace`. The replace is atomic but the sequence is not; Flatline runs its voices as parallel cheval processes, so two provider verdicts within the same second drop one row (dissent DISS-C-006). The store is a calibration signal, so the damage is a lost observation, not a wrong bound. (The dissent's symlink point is not a defect: `os.replace` replaces a planted link rather than writing through it.)
**Suggestion:** Take the same per-user flock the ledger writers use (issue #689) around the read-append-replace.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= pr/PR.md)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is the cycle-126 sprint-247 PR "full-size adapters, Bridgebuilder and Flatline — every size
decision derives from the resolved catalog entry" (65 files; `pr/head.diff`). The core of it is sound: the new
`loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py` policy module is small, pure and well tested; the provider context-limit class
(`ProviderContextLimitError`, not walked, observed-bound store, calibration command) is wired end to end and its e2e
tests pass; the Flatline per-voice budget and the generated `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT` map agree with the catalog
(`gen-adapter-maps.sh --check` is clean); the Bridgebuilder generated tables agree with the yaml for every entry.

Three defects block the merge. The first is in the dispatch path the PR is about: the per-hop input gate in
`cmd_invoke` still compares the raw character heuristic, not the estimate the pre-flight just accepted (which may be
the provider's `count_tokens` answer), so the D-1.4 count feature is defeated on the walk and a call the pre-flight
dispatched is skipped at every HTTP hop. The second is in Bridgebuilder: the default model becomes the alias `opus`
(and the personas `tiny` / `opus`) but the truncation budget tables are keyed by concrete ids and nothing in this PR
resolves aliases, so the default review runs with no per-model input clamp (200K, above cheval's 180K probed bound).
The third is in the retry layer: the one-shot output-budget shrink is silently lost when the provider's verdict
arrives on the last attempt, and the error degrades to a walkable `RetriesExhaustedError` — the exact outcome D-1.1b
forbids. Both dissent voices (Phase 2.5) found all three independently.

Process: `reviewer.md` is the PR description only — it carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no test or
fast-gate evidence, which is on its own an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED under this skill. Verification evidence I could
produce in this sandbox is listed under "Verification performed" (with the caveat that the workspace tree is a later
revision of the repository, not the PR's base).

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality — the walk gate ignores the pre-flight / counted estimate (cheval)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2119-2120` — the per-hop input gate recomputes `estimate_tokens(messages)` (the chars/3.5 heuristic) and compares it with the hop bound, while the pre-flight at `:1815-1845` may have replaced the estimate with the provider's `count_tokens` answer (`_walk_estimate`, `:1842`). A request the pre-flight dispatched on the count is skipped as ROUTING_MISS at every HTTP hop.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2119-2120` (also `:2090`, where the same loop's I1 fit uses `_walk_estimate`)
**Issue:** Concrete failing input under the default `probed` policy: a 1M-window head entry (`claude-opus-5`, probed 180,000), a prompt whose heuristic is 190,000 tokens and whose `count_tokens` answer is 175,000. Pre-flight: 190,000 ≥ 0.9 × 180,000 so the counter runs (`ceiling.py:409`), `est` becomes 175,000 ≤ 180,000 → `dispatch`, envelope `estimator.method: count_tokens`. Walk, hop 1: `_lookup_max_input_tokens` returns 180,000; `_estimated = estimate_tokens(messages)` = 190,000 > 180,000 → `ROUTING_MISS`, `continue`. Every HTTP fallback (same probed value) is skipped the same way; the call lands on `claude-headless` (6–10 min) or exits CHAIN_EXHAUSTED. The same happens on a 200K entry after the pre-flight I1 shrink: the hop fit (`:2090`) uses the counted 170,000 → `max_tokens` 30,000 → derived bound 170,000, then the gate compares the heuristic 190,000 against it.
**Why This Matters:** D-1.4 ("near the bound the provider's count replaces the estimate") is the reason the count endpoint exists; it only works at the pre-flight, and the two gates inside one loop disagree with each other. The envelope then records `preflight_decision: dispatch` with `method: count_tokens` next to a `ROUTING_MISS` quoting the heuristic — contradictory telemetry an operator cannot act on. No test covers the default-policy case with a count below the heuristic (`test_opt_in_count_endpoint_is_authoritative` runs under the `derived` opt-in where the bound is 936,000, so the heuristic passes anyway). Dissent: DISS-001 (gpt-5.5-pro), DISS-C-001 (claude-headless), both BLOCKING.
**Required Fix:** Use the walk estimate at the hop gate — `_estimated = _walk_estimate if _walk_estimate is not None else estimate_tokens(messages)` — and add an e2e row (default policy, counter → 175,000, heuristic ≈ 190,000, head entry 1M) asserting one dispatch and no ROUTING_MISS.

**Example:**
```python
# Current (problematic) — cheval.py:2118-2120
from loa_cheval.providers.base import estimate_tokens
_estimated = estimate_tokens(messages)
if _estimated > _input_threshold:

# Should be
_estimated = _walk_estimate if _walk_estimate is not None else estimate_tokens(messages)
if _estimated > _input_threshold:
```

### 2. Functionality — Bridgebuilder's alias defaults have no token budget

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:172` — the built-in default model becomes the alias `opus` (and `personas/quick.md:2` → `tiny`, `personas/security.md:2` → `opus`), but the budget tables the reviewer consults are keyed by concrete ids only (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/truncation.generated.ts:19` onward; no alias map is generated by `scripts/gen-bb-registry.ts`), and `core/truncation.ts` is not touched by this PR. `getTokenBudget("opus")` falls through to `TOKEN_BUDGETS["default"]` and `effectiveInputBudget(200_000, "opus")` returns the unclamped 200,000 because the id is unknown.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:172` and `:176`
**Issue:** Before this PR the default was `claude-opus-4-7` with `maxInputTokens` 128,000: a known id, clamped to min(128,000, 160,000). After it, a default-config review of a large PR prepares up to 200,000 tokens of diff for a model whose cheval input bound is the 180,000 probed value (`model-config.yaml`), so cheval pre-empts it with CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE (exit 7) where it used to dispatch. The PR's own test only asserts the string (`__tests__/config.test.ts:161`: `assert.equal(config.model, "opus")`) and `truncation.test.ts` asserts budgets for concrete ids only; nothing exercises `getTokenBudget("opus")`. The cheval delegate resolves the alias for dispatch, so the model itself is fine — the budget lookup is what breaks. (The workspace copy of `truncation.ts` already carries an alias-resolving `budgetId()` annotated "cycle-126 sprint-250 round 2", i.e. a later fix for exactly this gap; it is not part of this change.)
**Why This Matters:** The default configuration — what every operator who did not pin a model gets — regresses from "truncated and reviewed" to "pre-empted" on exactly the large PRs Bridgebuilder exists for, and `maxInputTokens: 200_000` (`:176`) is above the catalog's dispatchable bound for the alias target even when the id is known.
**Required Fix:** Either keep concrete ids as the default/persona values, or have `gen-bb-registry.ts` emit the yaml `aliases:` block as a generated alias map and resolve it in `getTokenBudget` / `effectiveInputBudget` (and `isReasoningClass`, which keys `GENERATED_REASONING[modelId]` by concrete id too); set the input default at or under the alias target's generated `maxInput` (160,000); add a test that `getTokenBudget("opus")` equals the budget of the `opus` target.

### 3. Error handling — the retry layer's one-shot shrink is lost on the final attempt

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/retry.py:494-495` — the context-limit arm does `request = replace(request, max_tokens=room)` then `continue` without checking that an iteration remains and without setting `last_typed_error`. When the `ProviderContextLimitError` arrives on the last pass of `for attempt in range(max_retries + 1)` — `retry.max_retries: 0` in config, or three earlier 429/503 backoffs — the loop ends and `:531` raises `RetriesExhaustedError`, so cheval's `except ProviderContextLimitError` (`cheval.py:2247`) never fires.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/retry.py:494-495` (and `:531`)
**Issue:** The shrunk request is never sent; the typed verdict degrades to a generic `RetriesExhaustedError`, which cheval's walk path treats as walkable: the same oversized payload goes to the next voice, no `.run/ceiling-observed.json` row is written, and the operator never sees the calibration command. `last_error` is also stale or `None` in that record because this arm never assigns it. The new `test_ceiling_retry.py` only runs with `max_retries: 3` and a first-attempt error.
**Why This Matters:** Severity is the damage: it is exactly the D-1.1b invariant ("the provider's own size verdict ends the call — it is never walked") being broken; confidence is medium because the default `max_retries: 3` needs three prior transient failures to reach it, but a zero-retry configuration reaches it on the first error. Dissent: DISS-002 (gpt-5.5-pro), DISS-C-002 (claude-headless), both BLOCKING.
**Required Fix:** Perform the shrunk retry outside the attempt budget (one extra `adapter.complete()` after the shrink), or set `last_typed_error = e` and re-raise `e` when `attempt == max_retries`; add tests with `max_retries: 0` and with the context error on the final attempt.

---

## Observations

### 1. `_ceiling_unverified` is the head entry's flag but gates every hop

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1843` and `:2297` — the flag is computed once from the pre-flight on the head entry, then consulted on every hop's 429 arm (and `:2256` for the context-limit class). Under the `derived` opt-in, a 429 on a fallback hop (whose own probed bound the request may well be under, or which is calibrated) ends the call as `RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED` and records an observation against that fallback entry, instead of walking as before. The arm also treats every 429 the same, including an ordinary requests-per-minute limit that says nothing about the payload (dissent DISS-003/DISS-004/DISS-C-003).
**Suggestion:** Recompute the unverified zone per hop (`estimate > probed_ceiling` of that entry, and not calibrated) or clear the flag when leaving the head entry; consider distinguishing token-limit 429 bodies from RPM ones before refusing to walk.

### 2. `/loa` prints `ceiling: observed -1` from a zero-token observation row

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:811-819` — the jq reduction takes the `min` of `observed_input_tokens` without a positivity check, while cheval writes `observed_input_tokens: 0` when the gate is disabled and the provider message carries no numbers (`head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2005`: `int(_walk_estimate or 0)`). A row `{"observed_input_tokens": 0, "error_class": "PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT"}` yields `obs=0`, which passes the `^[0-9]+$` check, so the status line reads `ceiling: observed -1`. The Python reducer (`ceiling.py:252`) skips non-positive values, so the two readers disagree (dissent DISS-C-004).
**Suggestion:** Filter `observed_input_tokens > 0` in the jq, and do not append a row (or record `null`) when no positive observation exists.

### 3. Observed-bound store has an unlocked read-modify-write

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:279-299` — `load_observed` → append → `os.replace`. The replace is atomic but the sequence is not; Flatline runs its voices as parallel cheval processes, so two provider verdicts within the same second drop one row (dissent DISS-C-006). The store is a calibration signal, so the damage is a lost observation, not a wrong bound. (The dissent's symlink point is not a defect: `os.replace` replaces a planted link rather than writing through it.)
**Suggestion:** Take the same per-user flock the ledger writers use (issue #689) around the read-append-replace.

### 4. Flatline: every call kind now gets a 64K budget on 128K entries

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/flatline-orchestrator.sh:936-946` and `:1027` — `score` (a small JSON array) and review/skeptic alike pass `--max-tokens 64000` for `claude-opus-5`. The cycle-124 rationale this replaces ("the 600 s per-call timeout never meets a 64K-output generation") is removed without touching the per-call timeout, and on the adaptive-thinking Opus the budget is shared with thinking. A runaway or long-thinking generation now runs to the timeout and drops the voice where 16K bounded it.
**Suggestion:** Keep the cap per voice but let the mode lower it (`score` has no use for 64K), or document the timeout interaction in the SDD.

### 5. Health probe: any non-404 on `/models` is now "unhealthy"

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/anthropic_adapter.py:672` — `if status != 404: return False`. A gateway or proxy that does not serve `GET /v1/models` and answers 403/405/501 (or an `http_get` transport 503) is reported unhealthy without ever trying the one-token message that the previous probe used, so the breaker/status surfaces a false negative for proxied Anthropic endpoints.
**Suggestion:** Fall back to the message probe on any non-2xx other than an authentication error.

### 6. Long-context threshold ignores cache tokens

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py:168` — eligibility tests `input_tokens > threshold` only, although the function then multiplies `cr_cost` / `cw_cost` by the input multiplier (it knows cache traffic is input-side) and the provider's published 1M rule counts the whole prompt. A request of 1,000 uncached + 250,000 cache-read tokens is billed at the base tier, `long_context` is not set on the ledger row, and `cost-report.sh` undercounts exactly the cache-heavy workloads most likely to exceed 200K (dissent DISS-005, DISS-C-005). Confidence medium because the catalog marks the tier `verified: false`.
**Suggestion:** Test `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens > threshold`, and pin it in `test_long_context_pricing.py`.

### 7. Estimator parity claim does not hold on hosts with tiktoken

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib-multipass.sh:95-98` — the comment says the Anthropic pass uses "the same chars / 3.5 bound cheval applies", but cheval's `estimate_tokens` (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:931`) prefers the cl100k encoding for every provider when tiktoken is installed, and `estimate_input` (`base.py:1000`) labels an Anthropic estimate `method: tiktoken`. The two estimators diverge on exactly the hosts the comment describes.
**Suggestion:** Either make `estimate_tokens` provider-aware or correct the comment.

### 8. Dead branch in `fit_max_tokens`

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:144-145` — `room >= requested` is equivalent to `estimate + requested <= context_window`, which the first branch already returned on; this arm is unreachable. SIMPLICITY[delete].

### 9. Long-context tier only on the 5-family

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:541` (claude-opus-4-8, `context_window: 1000000`) and `:744` (claude-sonnet-4-6, also 1M) — these 1M-window entries carry no `pricing.long_context`, and `head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:320` locks that in. If the published premium applies to them, >200K requests on these ids are under-billed by 2×.
**Suggestion:** State the applicability in the yaml comment or add the block.

### 10. Raw provider message in the calibration exit

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2021` and `:2029` — `str(_exc)` is interpolated into `models_failed[].message_redacted` and the stderr `_error_json` line without redaction in this closure (dissent DISS-C-007). This matches the existing arms (every other `except` does the same and relies on the modelinv emit-time redaction), and the context-limit body is a fixed-shape message with numbers, so the exposure is the stderr line only.
**Suggestion:** Route the stderr message through the shared redactor like the envelope path.

### 11. Test hygiene

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_write_catalog.py:66-69` — a `… if False else …` expression leaves the first `write_catalog` call dead code inside a `pytest.raises`; only the else branch runs.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:295-296` — `assert A == … or derived.basis in ("calibrated", "i1")` is near-tautological for the shipped entries (every uncalibrated 1M row takes the first disjunct trivially; the 200K rows satisfy the second); it does not pin the derived value.

### 12. Complexity

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1805-1862` and `:1994-2037` — `cmd_invoke` grows by ~250 lines (a nested closure with `nonlocal`, a 60-line pre-flight branch). The policy module itself is lean (`ceiling.py`: Lean already. Ship.). SIMPLICITY[shrink]: extract the pre-flight gate call into a helper returning `(decision, outcome)`; net: -40 lines possible in `cmd_invoke`.

---

## Cross-Model Observations

Phase 2.5 ran `adversarial-review.sh --type review --sprint-id sprint-1 --diff-file pr/head.diff` with two voices:
primary `gpt-5.5-pro` (status `reviewed`) and companion `claude-headless` (`succeeded`, `counted_as:
independent_voice`). 12 findings (8 BLOCKING, 4 ADVISORY). Disposition:

- DISS-001 / DISS-C-001 (walk gate uses the heuristic) → counted as Change 1.
- DISS-002 / DISS-C-002 (retry shrink lost on the final attempt) → counted as Change 3.
- DISS-003 / DISS-004 / DISS-C-003 (`_ceiling_unverified` head-only; every 429 refused while unverified) → Observation 1 (MEDIUM: opt-in zone, two coincident failures needed).
- DISS-005 / DISS-C-005 (cache tokens excluded from the long-context threshold) → Observation 6.
- DISS-C-004 (zero-token observation row) → Observation 2. DISS-C-006 (unlocked store; symlink) → Observation 3 (symlink part rejected: `os.replace` does not write through a link). DISS-C-007 (unredacted stderr) → Observation 10.
- Neither voice raised the Bridgebuilder alias budget defect (Change 2); it stands on my own reading.

## Rejected dissent payloads

None. `metadata.rejected_summary` is empty and both sidecars (`adversarial-rejected-review.jsonl`, companion: null) hold no rows.

---

## Acceptance Criteria Check

Sprint criterion (sprint.md): "review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict".

### Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

| Criterion | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| D-1.1 input bound is a policy over the entry (I1/I2, probed default, derived opt-in, legacy switch) | Pass | `ceiling.py` + `test_ceiling_policy.py` (all pass on the overlay) |
| D-1.1b provider verdict not walked, observed store, calibration command | **Fail** | `test_ceiling_e2e.py` passes, but the final-attempt path walks the payload (Change 3); Obs. 1–3 |
| D-1.4 count endpoint replaces the estimate near the bound | **Fail** | Pre-flight only; the walk gate re-compares the heuristic (Change 1) |
| D-1.3 output defaults per provider, temperature off the wire | Pass | adapters + `test_full_size_adapter_defaults.py`; no other adapter puts `request.temperature` on the wire |
| D-1.2 beta headers allowlisted, one header | Pass | regex anchored; ConfigError on anything else |
| D-1.5 Bridgebuilder budgets/reasoning from the yaml, alias default | **Fail** | generated tables consistent with yaml; alias default has no budget (Change 2) |
| D-1.6 Flatline per-voice budget from the catalog | Pass (Obs. 4) | `flatline-max-tokens.bats` 6/6 pass; `gen-adapter-maps.sh --check` OK |
| D-1.7 health probe without a retired id | Pass (Obs. 5) | |
| D-1.9 long-context pricing + ledger flag + cost-report count | Pass (Obs. 6, 9) | `test_long_context_pricing.py`, `cost-report.bats` CR-8 pass |
| `/loa` surfaces the bound | Pass (Obs. 2) | |
| Implementation report carries `## AC Verification` with file:line evidence | **Fail** | `reviewer.md` is the PR title + "65 file(s) in scope" |

---

## Verification performed

- Workspace caveat: the checked-out tree is neither `pr/base` nor `pr/head` (it is a later revision of the repository), so the head could not be reconstructed exactly. Tests ran on an overlay of the 65 head files over that tree, with the tree's superset `types.py` to satisfy newer untouched modules.
- Python: 163 passed, 1 failed — `test_advisor_tier_points_at_opus_5`, a pre-existing test (present in `pr/base`) that reads the live sandbox `.loa.config.yaml`; not a PR defect.
- bats: `flatline-max-tokens.bats` 6/6, `multipass-estimator.bats` 3/3, `cost-report.bats` CR-8 pass.
- `gen-adapter-maps.sh --check`: generated maps match the head yaml. Generated Bridgebuilder tables (`truncation.generated.ts`, `config.generated.ts`) checked against the yaml for every entry: consistent (maxOutput = min(declared, 32K), reasoning flag = thinking_adaptive ∨ thinking_traces, maxInput = ceiling − 20K). `dist/` artefacts carry the same reasoning flags as the sources.
- FAST-GATE: the report gives no evidence that `tsc --noEmit` / the formatter ran; the rebuilt `dist/.build-manifest.json` implies a build, but it could not be verified here (no node_modules).

---

## Security Checklist

- [x] No hardcoded secrets or credentials (the retired snapshot id is gone from the probe; the store holds counts only)
- [x] Input validation and sanitization present (beta-header allowlist is anchored — prevents header injection, CWE-113; `_long_context_fields` rejects malformed blocks; env knobs parsed defensively)
- [x] Authentication/authorization correct (count_tokens reuses the adapter's own headers/key; no new credential path)
- [x] No SQL/XSS injection vulnerabilities (n/a)
- [x] Dependencies secure (no new dependencies)
- [x] Error messages don't leak sensitive data (provider messages pass through the existing emit-time redaction; see Obs. 10 for the stderr line)

---

## Code Quality Summary

**Strengths:**
- `ceiling.py` is a clean, pure, well-named policy module with every basis labelled and an envelope projection; its unit tests are thorough.
- The provider context-limit class is typed end to end (adapter → retry → cheval → envelope → `/loa`), with the calibration command surfaced in three places.
- Generated artefacts (shell maps, TS tables, dist) are regenerated and consistent with the catalog.

**Areas for Improvement:**
- The two gates inside `cmd_invoke`'s walk loop must read the same estimate (Change 1).
- Alias-valued defaults need alias-aware budget lookups (Change 2).
- The retry layer's shrink must not depend on an iteration remaining (Change 3).
- The implementation report must carry the AC walkthrough and fast-gate evidence.

---

## Next Steps

1. Address the three Changes Required above (and Observations 1–3 while in the same files).
2. Add the missing tests (default-policy count rescue; `getTokenBudget("opus")`; `max_retries: 0` shrink).
3. Update `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md` with an `## AC Verification` section (every AC, `file:line` evidence, test and fast-gate output).
4. Request another review via `/review-sprint sprint-1`.

**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2119-2120` (also `:2090`, where the same loop's I1 fit uses `_walk_estimate`)

# Reviewer concerns — sprint-1 (cycle-126 full-size adapters PR)

Phase 2 notes for the cross-model dissent. Cite head/<path>:<line>.

1. cheval.py walk-loop input gate (head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2118-2120) re-estimates with the raw
   heuristic `estimate_tokens(messages)` while the pre-flight (1815-1845) may have replaced the estimate with the
   provider's count_tokens value (`_walk_estimate`). Under the default `probed` policy, a prompt whose heuristic is
   above 180K but whose count is under it is dispatched by the pre-flight and then skipped per hop as ROUTING_MISS.
2. retry.py (head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/retry.py:472-497): the one-shot output-budget shrink does
   `continue`; on the final loop iteration this falls through to RetriesExhaustedError, so the typed
   ProviderContextLimitError is lost (walked by cheval as RetriesExhausted, no observed-bound record).
3. cheval.py `_ceiling_unverified` is computed from the head entry only (1842) but consulted on every hop's 429 arm
   (2297), so a fallback hop's 429 under the derived opt-in ends the chain instead of walking.
4. loa-status.sh `_anthropic_ceiling_json` (head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:811-815) treats an
   `observed_input_tokens: 0` row (cheval writes 0 when the gate is disabled and the message carries no numbers)
   as a bound and prints `ceiling: observed -1`; the Python reducer skips non-positive values.
5. ceiling.py record_observed (head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:278-299): read-modify-write of
   the store with no lock; parallel Flatline voices can drop each other's rows.
6. flatline-orchestrator.sh: every call kind (including `score`) now gets 64000 max_tokens for a 128K entry; the
   cycle-124 rationale (600 s per-call timeout never meets a 64K generation) is reverted without a timeout change.
7. Bridgebuilder default `model: "opus"` (config.ts) and persona `# model: tiny|opus`: check getTokenBudget/
   effectiveInputBudget resolve the alias; otherwise the default budget (100K maxInput) applies instead of 160K.
8. fit_max_tokens lines 144-145 are unreachable (the condition is implied by the first branch).

3. cheval.py `_ceiling_unverified` is computed from the head entry only (1842) but consulted on every hop's 429 arm

   `observed_input_tokens: 0` row (cheval writes 0 when the gate is disabled and the message carries no numbers)

MAX_DEPTH=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case $1 in
    --no-symlinks) FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=false; shift ;;
    --max-depth) MAX_DEPTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) OUTPUT_JSON=true; shift ;;

  FIND_OPTS=(-maxdepth "$MAX_DEPTH" "${FIND_OPTS[@]}")

1	"""Input-bound policy over a catalog entry (cycle-126 Sprint 1, PRD FR-1.1,
     2	SDD D-1.1 / D-1.1b).
     3	
     4	The bound a request may carry to a model is not one literal; it is decided
     5	from the entry and the request:
     6	
     7	  I1  ``estimate + max_tokens_on_wire ≤ context_window`` — the provider's
     8	      hard invariant. ``fit_max_tokens`` shrinks the output budget to a
     9	      4,096 floor before anything is refused; ``input_bound`` never returns
    10	      more than ``context_window − max_tokens``.
    11	  I2  the input bound proper:
    12	        calibrated entry (``ceiling_calibration.calibrated_at`` set) →
    13	            its ``effective_input_ceiling`` (a measurement);
    14	        uncalibrated entry, default policy ``probed`` →
    15	            ``probed_ceiling`` (the last measured value the catalog ships);
    16	        uncalibrated entry, policy ``derived`` (``LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived``) →
    17	            ``context_window − max_tokens`` (the catalog's own arithmetic);
    18	        an observed provider limit (``.run/ceiling-observed.json``, written by
    19	            the self-correction) caps an uncalibrated bound at
    20	            ``observed − 1`` until calibration;
    21	        ``LOA_CHEVAL_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS`` lowers any bound (basis ``guard``);
    22	        ``LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_CEILING=1`` → today's single literal, no I1.
    23	
    24	Every basis is named in the decision so the envelope, the log line and the
    25	tests can say why a request was allowed or refused. Entries without any
    26	ceiling field (v2 shapes, CLI hops) have no bound here (``None``).
    27	"""
    28	from __future__ import annotations
    29	
    30	import datetime as _dt
    31	import json
    32	import os
    33	import re
    34	import tempfile
    35	from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
    36	from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional
    37	
    38	FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS = 4_096
    39	_TRUTHY = ("1", "true", "yes", "on")
    40	
    41	
    42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    43	class CeilingDecision:
    44	    value: int
    45	    basis: str  # calibrated | probed | derived | observed | i1 | guard | legacy
    46	    calibrated: bool
    47	    probed: Optional[int]
    48	    derived: Optional[int]
    49	    observed: Optional[int] = None
    50	    policy: str = "probed"
    51	
    52	
    53	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    54	class MaxTokensFit:
    55	    max_tokens: Optional[int]  # None ⇒ even the floor does not fit
    56	    shrunk_from: Optional[int]
    57	
    58	
    59	def policy_from_env() -> str:
    60	    """``legacy`` (kill switch wins) | ``derived`` (opt-in) | ``probed`` (default)."""
    61	    if os.environ.get("LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_CEILING", "").strip().lower() in _TRUTHY:
    62	        return "legacy"
    63	    if os.environ.get("LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING", "").strip().lower() == "derived":
    64	        return "derived"
    65	    return "probed"
    66	
    67	
    68	def _pos_int(value: Any) -> Optional[int]:
    69	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value <= 0:
    70	        return None
    71	    return value
    72	
    73	
    74	def _guard_from_env() -> Optional[int]:
    75	    raw = os.environ.get("LOA_CHEVAL_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS", "").strip()
    76	    if not raw:
    77	        return None
    78	    try:
    79	        n = int(raw)
    80	    except ValueError:
    81	        return None
    82	    return n if n > 0 else None
    83	
    84	
    85	def is_calibrated(entry: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    86	    cal = entry.get("ceiling_calibration")
    87	    return isinstance(cal, dict) and bool(cal.get("calibrated_at"))
    88	
    89	
    90	def input_bound(
    91	    entry: Dict[str, Any],
    92	    *,
    93	    max_tokens: int,
    94	    observed: Optional[int] = None,
    95	    policy: Optional[str] = None,
    96	) -> Optional[CeilingDecision]:
    97	    """The largest input (tokens) this request may carry, with its basis."""
    98	    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
    99	        return None
   100	    ceiling = _pos_int(entry.get("effective_input_ceiling"))
   101	    probed = _pos_int(entry.get("probed_ceiling")) or ceiling
   102	    if ceiling is None and probed is None:
   103	        return None  # v2 entry / CLI hop — no bound from this module
   104	    cw = _pos_int(entry.get("context_window"))
   105	    derived = (cw - int(max_tokens)) if cw else None
   106	    if derived is not None and derived <= 0:
   107	        derived = 0
   108	    policy = policy or policy_from_env()
   109	    calibrated = is_calibrated(entry)
   110	
   111	    if policy == "legacy":
   112	        return CeilingDecision(value=ceiling or probed or 0, basis="legacy", calibrated=calibrated,
   113	                               probed=probed, derived=derived, observed=observed, policy=policy)
   114	
   115	    if calibrated and ceiling is not None:
   116	        value, basis = ceiling, "calibrated"
   117	    elif policy == "derived" and derived is not None:
   118	        value, basis = derived, "derived"
   119	    else:
   120	        value, basis = (probed or ceiling or 0), "probed"
   121	
   122	    if not calibrated and observed is not None and _pos_int(observed) and observed - 1 < value:
   123	        value, basis = observed - 1, "observed"
   124	
   125	    if derived is not None and derived < value:  # I1 — never promise more than the window minus the output
   126	        value, basis = derived, "i1"
   127	
   128	    guard = _guard_from_env()
   129	    if guard is not None and guard < value:
   130	        value, basis = guard, "guard"
   131	
   132	    return CeilingDecision(value=value, basis=basis, calibrated=calibrated, probed=probed,
   133	                           derived=derived, observed=observed, policy=policy)
   134	
   135	
   136	def fit_max_tokens(*, context_window: int, estimate: int, requested: int) -> MaxTokensFit:
   137	    """I1 auto-shrink: keep ``requested`` when it fits, else the largest budget
   138	    that fits (never below the floor); ``None`` when even the floor does not."""
   139	    if estimate + requested <= context_window:
   140	        return MaxTokensFit(max_tokens=requested, shrunk_from=None)
   141	    room = context_window - estimate
   142	    if room >= FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS:
   143	        return MaxTokensFit(max_tokens=room, shrunk_from=requested)
   144	    if 0 < requested < FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS and room >= requested:
   145	        return MaxTokensFit(max_tokens=requested, shrunk_from=None)
   146	    return MaxTokensFit(max_tokens=None, shrunk_from=requested)
   147	
   148	
   149	# --- provider context-limit messages (D-1.1b) ---------------------------------
   150	
   151	# The two shapes the Anthropic Messages API uses for an oversize request; the
   152	# numbers are the provider's own count, more accurate than any estimate.

   355	def gate(
   356	    entry: Dict[str, Any],
   357	    *,
   358	    estimate: GateEstimate,
   359	    requested_max_tokens: int,
   360	    cli_override: Optional[int] = None,
   361	    observed: Optional[int] = None,
   362	    policy: Optional[str] = None,
   363	    counter: Optional[Callable[[], Optional[int]]] = None,
   364	) -> GateOutcome:
   365	    """Decide dispatch / warn / preempt for the head entry.
   366	
   367	    Order: I1 (shrink the output budget to fit the window; preempt only when
   368	    the 4,096 floor does not fit) → I2 bound (``input_bound``; the CLI
   369	    override lowers it) → near the bound, a provider count replaces the
   370	    estimate when ``counter`` is given → compare. Above the probed bound but
   371	    under the derived one (reachable only under the opt-in) a count or a
   372	    ``low`` estimate ``warn``s, a ``high`` estimate ``preempt``s with the
   373	    calibration command. ``legacy`` policy: no I1, no count, the literal.
   374	    """
   375	    policy = policy or policy_from_env()
   376	    max_tokens = int(requested_max_tokens)
   377	    shrunk_from: Optional[int] = None
   378	    cw = _pos_int(entry.get("context_window")) if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
   379	
   380	    def _out(action: str, reason: str, decision: Optional[CeilingDecision], bound: Optional[int],
   381	             basis: Optional[str], est: GateEstimate, unverified: bool = False) -> GateOutcome:
   382	        return GateOutcome(action=action, reason=reason, estimate=est, decision=decision, bound=bound,
   383	                           basis=basis, max_tokens=max_tokens, shrunk_from=shrunk_from,
   384	                           unverified=unverified, policy=policy)
   385	
   386	    if policy != "legacy" and cw:
   387	        fit = fit_max_tokens(context_window=cw, estimate=estimate.tokens, requested=max_tokens)
   388	        if fit.max_tokens is None:
   389	            return _out("preempt", f"I1: estimated {estimate.tokens} input tokens + the {FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS} output floor "
   390	                        f"exceed context_window {cw}", None, None, "i1", estimate)
   391	        if fit.shrunk_from is not None:
   392	            max_tokens, shrunk_from = fit.max_tokens, fit.shrunk_from
   393	
   394	    decision = input_bound(entry, max_tokens=max_tokens, observed=observed, policy=policy)
   395	    if decision is None:
   396	        if cli_override is not None and 0 < int(cli_override) < estimate.tokens:
   397	            return _out("preempt", f"estimated {estimate.tokens} input tokens > {int(cli_override)} "
   398	                        f"(--max-input-tokens)", None, int(cli_override), "cli_override", estimate)
   399	        return _out("dispatch", "no input bound for this entry", None, None, None, estimate)
   400	    bound, basis = decision.value, decision.basis
   401	    if cli_override is not None and 0 < int(cli_override) < bound:
   402	        bound, basis = int(cli_override), "cli_override"
   403	
   404	    est = estimate
   405	    probed = decision.probed
   406	    in_unverified_zone = bool(policy == "derived" and not decision.calibrated and probed and est.tokens > probed)

   408	    # count settles a `high` estimate — the provider's count is authoritative.
   409	    if policy != "legacy" and counter is not None and (est.tokens >= COUNT_NEAR_BOUND * bound or in_unverified_zone):
   410	        counted = counter()
   411	        if _pos_int(counted):
   412	            est = replace(est, tokens=int(counted), method="count_tokens", uncertainty="none")
   413	
   414	    if est.tokens > bound:
   415	        return _out("preempt", f"estimated {est.tokens} input tokens > {bound} input bound ({basis})",
   416	                    decision, bound, basis, est)
   417	
   418	    if policy == "derived" and not decision.calibrated and probed and est.tokens > probed:
   419	        model = entry.get("model_id") or entry.get("_model_id") or "<model>"
   420	        if est.method == "count_tokens" or est.uncertainty == "low":
   421	            return _out("warn", f"estimated {est.tokens} input tokens above the probed bound {probed} "
   422	                        f"(uncalibrated; {est.method}, uncertainty {est.uncertainty}) — proceeding under the "
   423	                        f"derived bound {bound}; calibrate: {PROBE_COMMAND.format(model=model)}",
   424	                        decision, bound, basis, est, unverified=True)
   425	        return _out("preempt", f"estimated {est.tokens} input tokens above the probed bound {probed} with a "
   426	                    f"high-uncertainty estimate ({est.method}); calibrate first: "
   427	                    f"{PROBE_COMMAND.format(model=model)}", decision, bound, basis, est)
   428	    return _out("dispatch", "under the input bound", decision, bound, basis, est)

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""ceiling-probe-live.py — binary-search the safe input size for an Anthropic model.
     3	
     4	cycle-124 Sprint 1 Task 1.8 (SDD §2.5 / §6). The catalog ships
     5	`effective_input_ceiling: 180000` as `kf_derived` (the streaming-probed
     6	KF-002 ceiling). This probe measures it on a real account under the same
     7	transport cheval uses (streaming) and emits a JSON record the operator pastes
     8	into grimoires/loa/reports/2026-09-17-cycle-124-catalog-evidence.md and into
     9	`ceiling_calibration` (source: empirical_probe, calibrated_at, sample_size).
    10	
    11	Usage:
    12	  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --model claude-opus-5 \
    13	      [--max-tokens-probe 200000] [--min-tokens-probe 32000] [--budget-usd 1.5] \
    14	      [--output probe.json]
    15	
    16	Exit codes: 0 probe completed · 1 a call failed for a non-size reason ·
    17	2 usage · 3 the budget cap stopped the bisection (`partial: true` — the
    18	record is still written but is NOT full evidence). A call is OK when the
    19	stream reaches `message_stop`
    20	without an error event — NOT when a text block arrives: default-on thinking
    21	(Opus 5 / Fable) can spend a small `max_tokens` entirely on reasoning, which
    22	is a budget outcome, not a size failure (review round-1 medium 7). Each call
    23	asks for up to 1024 output tokens and records `stop_reason`; the cost is
    24	still dominated by input: 200K tokens on Opus 5 ≈ $1.00 per call; the budget
    25	cap stops the search (largest OK so far is still reported, `partial: true`,
    26	exit 3).
    27	
    28	Never run this from a test without LOA_RUN_LIVE_TESTS=1 — it spends money.
    29	"""
    30	
    31	from __future__ import annotations
    32	
    33	import argparse
    34	import datetime as dt
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import sys
    38	import urllib.error
    39	import urllib.request
    40	
    41	API = "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages"
    42	_PRICE_IN = {"claude-opus-5": 5_000_000, "claude-fable-5-1": 10_000_000, "claude-sonnet-5": 2_000_000,
    43	             "claude-opus-4-8": 5_000_000, "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001": 1_000_000}
    44	_FILLER = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. "  # ≈ 10 tokens
    45	
    46	
    47	def _probe_once(model: str, tokens: int, key: str) -> tuple[bool, str, str | None]:
    48	    """Stream one request with ≈`tokens` input tokens.
    49	
    50	    Returns (ok, detail, stop_reason): ok iff the stream reached `message_stop`
    51	    with no error event — the request was accepted at this size whatever the
    52	    model chose to do with its output budget."""
    53	    body = {
    54	        "model": model, "max_tokens": 1024, "stream": True,
    55	        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": _FILLER * (tokens // 10) + "\n\nReply: ok."}],
    56	    }
    57	    req = urllib.request.Request(
    58	        API, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), method="POST",
    59	        headers={"x-api-key": key, "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01", "content-type": "application/json",
    60	                 "accept": "text/event-stream"},
    61	    )
    62	    try:
    63	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as resp:
    64	            saw_stop, stop_reason = False, None
    65	            for raw in resp:
    66	                line = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
    67	                if not line.startswith("data: "):
    68	                    continue
    69	                try:
    70	                    event = json.loads(line[6:])
    71	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
    72	                    continue
    73	                kind = event.get("type")
    74	                if kind == "error":
    75	                    return False, line[:300], None
    76	                if kind == "message_delta":
    77	                    stop_reason = (event.get("delta") or {}).get("stop_reason") or stop_reason
    78	                if kind == "message_stop":
    79	                    saw_stop = True
    80	            if saw_stop:
    81	                return True, "", stop_reason
    82	            return False, "stream ended before message_stop (transport / truncation class)", stop_reason
    83	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    84	        detail = e.read().decode(errors="replace")[:300]
    85	        if e.code in (400, 413) and ("too long" in detail or "exceed" in detail or "maximum" in detail):
    86	            return False, f"HTTP {e.code}: {detail}", None
    87	        raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {e.code} (non-size failure): {detail}")
    88	    except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) as e:
    89	        return False, f"transport: {e}", None
    90	
    91	
    92	_DEFAULT_CATALOG = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
    93	                                ".claude", "defaults", "model-config.yaml")
    94	_TIERS = ("unverified", "1", "2", "3", "4", "custom")
    95	
    96	
    97	def _indent(line: str) -> int:
    98	    return len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
    99	
   100	
   101	def write_catalog(text: str, model: str, *, ceiling: int, calibrated_at: str, sample_size: int,
   102	                  tier: str = "unverified", itpm: int | None = None) -> str:
   103	    """cycle-126 FR-1.1 (SDD D-1.1): fold one probe result into the catalog
   104	    TEXT — a line-level edit inside the model's block so every comment and
   105	    every other entry stay byte-identical. Sets `effective_input_ceiling`,
   106	    `ceiling_calibration` (source empirical_probe, calibrated_at, sample_size)
   107	    and `account_limits` (tier, itpm). Raises ValueError when the block or a
   108	    required field is missing (never guesses a location)."""
   109	    if tier not in _TIERS:
   110	        raise ValueError(f"tier must be one of {_TIERS}, got {tier!r}")
   111	    lines = text.split("\n")
   112	    start = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.rstrip() == f"      {model}:"), None)
   113	    if start is None:
   114	        raise ValueError(f"{model}: no `      {model}:` block in the catalog")
   115	    end = start + 1
   116	    while end < len(lines) and (lines[end].strip() == "" or _indent(lines[end]) > 6):
   117	        end += 1
   118	    block = lines[start:end]
   119	
   120	    def _find(prefix: str, indent: int) -> int:
   121	        for i, l in enumerate(block):
   122	            if _indent(l) == indent and l.strip().startswith(prefix):
   123	                return i
   124	        raise ValueError(f"{model}: `{prefix.rstrip(':')}` not found in the entry")
   125	
   126	    def _set_scalar(i: int, key: str, value: str) -> None:
   127	        # keep an inline comment when the line carries one
   128	        comment = ""
   129	        if "#" in block[i]:
   130	            comment = "   #" + block[i].split("#", 1)[1]
   131	        block[i] = f"{' ' * _indent(block[i])}{key}: {value}{comment}"
   132	
   133	    _set_scalar(_find("effective_input_ceiling:", 8), "effective_input_ceiling", str(int(ceiling)))
   134	
   135	    def _nested(head_prefix: str, wanted: dict) -> None:
   136	        h = _find(head_prefix, 8)
   137	        j = h + 1
   138	        seen = set()
   139	        while j < len(block) and (block[j].strip() == "" or _indent(block[j]) > 8):
   140	            key = block[j].strip().split(":", 1)[0]
   141	            if _indent(block[j]) == 10 and key in wanted:
   142	                _set_scalar(j, key, wanted[key])
   143	                seen.add(key)
   144	            j += 1
   145	        insert_at = j
   146	        while insert_at > h + 1 and block[insert_at - 1].strip() == "":
   147	            insert_at -= 1
   148	        for key, value in wanted.items():
   149	            if key not in seen:
   150	                block.insert(insert_at, f"          {key}: {value}")
   151	                insert_at += 1
   152	
   153	    _nested("ceiling_calibration:", {"source": "empirical_probe", "calibrated_at": f'"{calibrated_at}"',
   154	                                     "sample_size": str(int(sample_size))})
   155	    try:
   156	        _find("account_limits:", 8)
   157	    except ValueError:
   158	        cal = _find("ceiling_calibration:", 8)
   159	        j = cal + 1
   160	        while j < len(block) and (block[j].strip() == "" or _indent(block[j]) > 8):
   161	            j += 1
   162	        block.insert(j, "        account_limits:")
   163	    _nested("account_limits:", {"tier": f'"{tier}"', "itpm": ("null" if itpm is None else str(int(itpm)))})
   164	    return "\n".join(lines[:start] + block + lines[end:])
   165	
   166	
   167	def _write_catalog_file(path: str, model: str, record: dict, tier: str, itpm: int | None) -> None:
   168	    import tempfile
   169	    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
   170	        text = fh.read()
   171	    new = write_catalog(text, model, ceiling=record["largest_ok_input_tokens"], calibrated_at=record["calibrated_at"],
   172	                        sample_size=record["sample_size"], tier=tier, itpm=itpm)

=== RUBRICS
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally scalable. Stateless services. Caching strategy. Database sharding ready. |
| 4 | Mostly scalable with minor bottlenecks. |
| 3 | Can scale vertically but horizontal scaling problematic. |
| 2 | Scalability issues. Single points of failure. |
| 1 | Cannot scale. Architecture prevents growth. |

### ARCH-RE: Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Fault tolerant. Graceful degradation. Retry logic. Health checks. Circuit breakers. |
| 4 | Good resilience with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic error handling but cascading failures possible. |
| 2 | Fragile. Single component failure affects system. |
| 1 | No resilience. Any failure brings down system. |

### ARCH-CX: Complexity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Simple, elegant design. Easy to understand. Well-documented patterns. |
| 4 | Reasonable complexity with minor over-engineering. |
| 3 | Moderately complex. Learning curve for new developers. |
| 2 | Overly complex. Hard to reason about. |
| 1 | Incomprehensible. Spaghetti architecture. |

### ARCH-ST: Standards Compliance
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Follows industry standards. Best practices throughout. Consistent patterns. |
| 4 | Mostly compliant with minor deviations. |
| 3 | Mixed adherence. Some non-standard approaches. |
| 2 | Frequent deviations from standards. |
| 1 | Ignores standards. Anti-patterns throughout. |

---

## Code Quality Rubrics

### CQ-RD: Readability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Self-documenting code. Clear naming. Consistent formatting. Easy to follow. |
| 4 | Good readability with minor issues. |
| 3 | Readable but inconsistent. Some confusing sections. |
| 2 | Hard to read. Poor naming. Inconsistent style. |
=== OUTPUT-SCHEMA
# Structured Finding Output Schema

Defines the JSONL output format for machine-parseable audit findings.

## Finding Schema

Each finding is a JSON object on a single line in the JSONL file.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "AuditFinding",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "category", "criterion", "severity", "score", "finding", "reasoning_trace", "confidence"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$",
      "description": "Unique finding ID (e.g., SEC-001, ARCH-042)"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["security", "architecture", "code_quality", "devops", "blockchain"],
      "description": "Audit category"
    },
    "criterion": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific rubric dimension (e.g., input_validation, modularity)"
    },
    "severity": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["CRITICAL", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "INFO"],
      "description": "Finding severity"
    },
    "score": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 5,
      "description": "Rubric score for this dimension"
    },
    "file": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "File path where issue was found"
    },
    "line": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Line number (if applicable)"
    },
    "code_snippet": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Relevant code excerpt"
    },
    "reasoning_trace": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "How the issue was discovered - analysis path and evidence"
    },
    "finding": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Clear description of the issue"
    },
    "critique": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific guidance for improvement"
    },
    "remediation": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Exact fix with code example if applicable"
    },
    "confidence": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["high", "medium", "low"],
      "description": "Confidence in the finding"
    },
